findings.title: rename() looks up the item by its place in the filtered list, then changes that place in the full list
findings.why: `render()` passes `i` from `visible().entries()`, which is the position in the filtered list. `rename()` then uses it as `todos[index]`, the position in the full list. With the 'Chưa xong' or 'Đã xong' filter on, renaming an item gives the new name to a different item and saves it. The user's data is changed without them noticing.
findings.fix: Pass the id, as `toggle` and `remove` do: `rename(t.id, input.value)`, then `const t = todos.find((x) => x.id === id)`. Add an app.test.js case that renames with a filter on.

findings.title: The new name reaches the page through innerHTML (policy-security@1#S3)
findings.why: `$('#message').innerHTML = `Đã đổi tên thành ${t.title}`` puts the user's text into HTML. A name like `` runs script. That name is saved, and a backup file can bring it back in through import.
findings.fix: Build the message with textContent. For example, create a `<b>` element, set its textContent to `t.title`, and append it after a text node. Or use `show(fill(MESSAGES.renamed, { title: t.title }))`.

findings.title: The rename message overwrites the 'not saved' warning (policy-ux@2#U1)
findings.why: `commit()` calls `show(persist(...).message)`, which shows MESSAGES.notSaved when the write fails. `rename()` then replaces #message with 'Đã đổi tên thành …'. The user is told the rename worked when it was never saved, and the data is lost silently on reload.
findings.fix: Show the rename message only when persist reported no problem. For example, have commit() return the persist result and call show(renamed) only if its message is null.

findings.title: Asks for confirmation on an action on one item (policy-ux@2#U2)
findings.why: U2 (v2) says actions on a single item happen at once and offer Undo for 10 seconds, with no confirmation dialog. This adds a native `confirm('Đổi tên việc này?')` on every rename. It is also the browser's dialog, not the app's own #confirm.
findings.fix: Remove the confirm and rename at once. If the team wants Undo, add it as the policy describes. Otherwise ask the UX owner whether rename needs it.

findings.title: Double-clicking the name also clicks the checkbox twice, and with a filter on the item disappears
findings.why: The span is inside the `<label>` with the checkbox. Each click of the double-click toggles the item, which calls commit() and re-renders. With the 'Chưa xong' or 'Đã xong' filter on, the first click moves the item out of view, so the user cannot rename it. Each double-click also writes to storage twice. I have not checked whether `dblclick` still fires on the span once the first click has re-rendered the list. If it does not, rename never starts at all. Check this in a browser.
findings.fix: Move the name span out of the `<label>`, or call preventDefault on click for the span. Or start editing from a separate 'Sửa' button.

findings.title: Rename cannot be reached with the keyboard (policy-ux@2#U5)
findings.why: Editing starts only on `ondblclick` on a span that cannot take focus. A keyboard-only user has no way to rename. U5 requires every control to work with the keyboard.
findings.fix: Add a focusable control with an aria-label, such as a 'Đổi tên' button, or start editing with Enter/F2 on a focusable name.

findings.title: No test for the new behaviour
findings.why: app.test.js runs app.js in a vm, but nothing covers rename: Enter, Esc, an empty name, or a filter being on. That is why the bug with the filtered position passed check.sh (44/44).
findings.fix: Add app.test.js cases: rename with a filter on, Esc keeps the old name, and the message shows the name as text.

findings.title: Clicking away leaves the edit box open
findings.why: There is no blur handler. The input stays until the next render, and the typed name is neither saved nor clearly cancelled.
findings.fix: On blur, either save (as Enter does) or call render() (as Esc does), and say which in the code.

findings.title: The new UI strings are hardcoded and not in MESSAGES
findings.why: Every other user-facing message lives in backup.js MESSAGES, and tests check them word for word. 'Đổi tên việc này?' and 'Đã đổi tên thành …' are left out of that.
findings.fix: Add `renamed` to MESSAGES and use fill().
